title: Redwood February 2026 - Leadership Update / All-Hands
summary: Leadership gave a concise update on Q4 results, FY26 priorities, hiring slowdowns in some areas and ramp in infra and sales, progress on Dedicated and Private releases, and compliance milestones. Action items include publishing a detailed Q1 operating plan, finishing SOC 2 readiness checklist, and shipping Dedicated perf benchmarks for customers. There were questions about timelines and tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated, and a brief recognition segment.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-26
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Rosa, Devon, Hannah, Luis, plus ~120 viewers (company)

Summary Section (auto):
Maya: Quick state of company and high level numbers, hiring plan, product progress, compliance.

Topics (auto):
- FY26 priorities and Q4 wrap
- Product launches: Dedicated GA cadence, Private pilot progress
- Compliance: SOC 2 timeline
- Sales/pricing adjustments
- People update and hiring pauses

Action items (auto):
- See action_items in metadata for owners and dates

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know it's busy week, so we'll kick off, um, high level right away. Quick housekeeping, recording this. Sorry if there's a little audio lag, I think my mic is, uh, doing something.

[00:28] Maya: Okay Q4 numbers first — we ended the quarter a bit below target on bookings, but ARR growth is healthy and net dollar retention improved, so, uh, mixed bag but fundamentally on track. We had particularly strong usage from a handful of AI-native customers and platform teams, so that's encouraging.

[01:05] Devon: Yeah just to add, some of the renewals slipped because procurement cycles stretched into Jan, that's on us to tighten. We're moving a new pricing playbook to address smaller PLG deals and also the enterprise commit paths.

[01:40] Ethan: From infra side, we saw latency improvements with the new kernel selection logic, CPU offload experiments helped reduce tail latency, so the runtime team is seeing good perf wins — still some work on memory for KV cache when we do larger context windows.

[02:12] Rosa: Product update: Dedicated is in beta with three customers, Private pilot ongoing with two regulated customers, console UX refresh almost ready for first lab, and Optimize has a new batching recommendation engine prototype.

[02:47] Maya: Whoa — quick Q on timeline — Dedicated GA?

[02:53] Rosa: We're targeting GA late April, I mean end of April, assuming the perf runs and docs land. There is a dependency on SOC 2 signoff for a few customers to move to dedicated and private.

[03:18] Hannah: Speaking of SOC 2 — audit kickoff is scheduled for the week of March 8, internal checklist goes out this Tuesday. We need owners for logging, SSO, and KMS pieces.

[03:42] Maya: Okay please make sure those owners are named, we can't have gaps.

[04:00] Luis: Research notes: quantization profiles look promising for Llama-like models at 4-bit int, we got a ~2.2x cost reduction in some workloads, but there's a small regen rate increase on long context outputs. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheets.

[04:33] Ethan: Quick caveat — those quant gains vary by architecture, and we shouldn't broadly advertise them until we have standardized metrics across our procurement of GPUs and the H100 vs A100 differences.

[05:00] Devon: On sales operations — we're seeing more RFPs ask specifically about VPC and on-prem options, so Private product needs clearer legal/comms on data residency. Also some buyers name Anthropic and OpenAI as comparison points during procurement cycles.

[05:35] Maya: Good note. We'll add a competitive page to the sales deck, but let's be careful with direct callouts.

[06:00] Audience question (via Q&A): "What's the plan for hiring in Q1?"

[06:12] Maya: We're pausing most new IC hiring for now — exception is infra, ops and sales where we have committed roles. The talent market is tight so we want to be strategic. Headcount plan will be published with the Q1 operating plan.

[06:42] Ethan: We'll keep a small hiring slate for infra and reliability — critical to keep perf momentum.

[07:05] Rosa: Product hiring will be minimal, but we'll prioritize PMs that help get Dedicated & Private to GA.

[07:25] Maya: Okay moving to monetization, Devon?

[07:30] Devon: We're adjusting unit economics with two levers: clearer reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated and usage tiers for hosted. We're also piloting a new sales incentive for net-new ARR that lands on dedicated contracts. We'll share the revised playbook next week.

[08:02] Audience chat comment (unattributed): "Can we get more detail on SSO and role-based access? Some of my team worried about RBAC in Private."

[08:15] Hannah: RBAC will be part of the Private PKG and the console refresh; SSO/SAML and SCIM integrations are on the checklist for SOC 2. We'll publish a migration guide.

[08:42] Maya: Any big customer escalations?

[08:50] Devon: A couple of mid-market customers reported increased token costs — we have a task force to analyze batching and caching settings per tenant. That's part of Optimize work.

[09:12] Luis: From an R&D angle, we're also experimenting with prefix caching heuristics to reduce regen and cost on chat workloads, early results good but needs more evaluation.

[09:45] Maya: Great. Quick shoutouts — Ops handled the incident last week very cleanly, Hannah and team — thanks.

[10:00] Hannah: Thanks — ops team worked cross-functionally with infra and SEs to reroute fallbacks, saved a lot of customer impact.

[10:20] Maya: Alright let's do a quick lightning updates round — one line each on top priorities. Ethan?

[10:25] Ethan: Perf benchmarks completion for Dedicated + autoscale playbook.

[10:30] Rosa: Console UX ship for beta labs and docs for Private.

[10:34] Devon: Pricing pilot rollout and AE training.

[10:38] Luis: Publish quantization benchmark spreadsheet and caveats.

[10:42] Hannah: SOC 2 readiness checklist and owner assignments.

[10:46] Maya: Okay recap — I'll share the operating plan early next week, please review and comment. Important: deadlines are tight because we have GA commitments to customers and the audit date.

[11:10] Audience question: "Will Dedicated GA be usable for on-prem / air-gapped customers?"

[11:20] Rosa: Not initially for air-gapped, but Private on-prem package is our path for those regulated use cases — there are separate install and legal steps.

[11:40] Maya: Closing notes: big thanks, I know it's a lot—transparency matters. We'll post the recording, slides, and the action item tracker.

[11:58] Maya: Alright, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

References shared in chat: "Q1 operating plan (link)", "Dedicated perf benchmarks (internal sheet link)", "SOC2 checklist (confluence link)"

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels, some garbled words around dense technical acronyms (KV cache, H100), overall medium quality.
